desc: Prove the structural lemma: complement of an interval graph has no induced 2K2 (an induced 2K2 would be an induced C4 in the interval graph, impossible by chordality), hence no induced P5; with positive weights a minimum path is chordless, so it has at most 3 edges.

Verify query formulas by case analysis: disjoint ⇒ direct edge optimal (positive weights); intersecting ⇒ best common neighbor (strictly left of both or strictly right of both) vs. opposite-side 3-edge paths; same-side 2-intermediate paths are dominated because the outer interval is then a common neighbor.
Validate formulas against Sample 1 by hand (answers 11, 6, -1 reproduced: query 1 uses common neighbor 3; query 2 direct edge; query 3 no candidates).

Implement input parsing and arrays bestR[r] / bestL[l] (min weight at each coordinate, size 2N+2), then prefix minima leftMin[x] = min W_i with R_i < x and suffix minima rightMin[x] = min W_i with L_i > x, using INF = 1<<62.
Answer queries in order: direct edge if disjoint; else min of common-neighbor and opposite-side 3-edge candidates with INF-safe adds; output -1 if no candidate.

Final review of edge cases in the code: touching endpoints count as intersecting (strict inequalities for disjointness), identical intervals, missing left/right candidates (pref[0] and suff[2N+1] are INF sentinels), 64-bit sums, fast I/O via buffer read, exactly Q output lines.

**Structural bound:** G is the complement of an interval graph. Interval graphs are chordal, so G has no induced 2K2 (= induced C4 in the complement), hence no induced P5. With positive weights, a minimum-weight path is chordless, so it has at most 3 edges. Any connected pair therefore has a ≤3-edge path, so the candidate enumeration is complete (no missed connectivity).

**3-edge case soundness:** For intersecting s,t, choosing `a` with `L_a > R_s` and `b` with `R_b < L_t` always yields valid edges s-a, a-b (since `R_b < L_t ≤ R_s < L_a`), b-t. If the chosen `a` were also disjoint from `t` (a chord), then `a` is a common neighbor and the 2-edge candidate is strictly cheaper, so the invalid-looking 3-edge value can never be the reported minimum. Same-side intermediate placements force a chord, as verified by case analysis on the endpoint orderings.

**Implementation details:** sentinel indices `pref[0]` and `suff[2N+1]` are INF; INF-safe additions; sums bounded by 4×10⁹ well within `1<<62`; O(N+Q) time and O(N) memory; hand-check against Sample 1 reproduces 11, 6, -1.
